Subject: Reserved capacity credit ladder & GPU-index safeguard — Acme.ai

Hi Anna,

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a proposed reserved-capacity structure that addresses Acme.ai's need for predictable throughput while protecting both parties from near-term GPU market volatility. The attached Commitment_Schedule.xlsx shows a 12-month commit with a tiered credit ladder tied to utilization and a pricing corridor tied to a quarterly GPU-index.

Key highlights (high-level):
- Baseline: guaranteed pool equivalent to 48 A100-equivalent slots, billed monthly.
- Credit ladder: partial month credits if utilization is under thresholds across rolling quarters (we included 3 tiers: 70%, 50%, 30% utilization).
- GPU-index safeguard: if the market GPU spot index moves >+25% vs baseline, Acme gets a one-time rebate credit to offset price pass-throughs up to a capped percentage.
- Decommit window: a staged decommit option at month 6 with a 60-day notice and step-down fees.

Two asks from Acme to move forward: confirmation of the ceiling on aggregate discounts and the approval path for any exceptions above the standard ladder. Can you confirm who on your procurement/legal side would own approvals for discount exceptions?

I'll loop in Finance for a sensitivity scan once I have your confirmation on the approval owner.

Attaching Commitment_Schedule.xlsx (sheet: summary + monthly phasing).

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Thanks Anna — good to know procurement will handle the standard approvals and CFO for exceptions. To answer your questions:
- The GPU-index safeguard we propose is a quarterly true-up credit applied to the committed invoice for that quarter (i.e., not retroactive outside the quarter), capped at 15% of the committed spend for the quarter. The goal is to smooth cost shocks without reopening whole-term economics.
- Maximum cumulative credits under the ladder: in our model the theoretical max (worst-case sustained low utilization) would be ~22% of annual committed spend, but realistic scenarios (one-off low quarters) usually end up under 8–10%.

I've asked David in Finance (cc) to run a sensitivity model on a few scenarios: high GPU price shock, multi-quarter low utilization, and a mixed case with staged decommit at month 6. I attached a first-draft term_sheet_v1.pdf with the proposed clause language for the index and decommit steps — this is intentionally conservative.

Next steps I propose:
- David: run sensitivity models and confirm whether the 15% quarterly cap is acceptable from a risk perspective.
- Karthik/Marcus: confirm whether the ladder fits the standard discount tiers or needs an exec exception.
- Anna/Procurement: indicate who will be the single point to route CFO-level sign-off if needed.

Thanks,
Naomi

[Attachment: term_sheet_v1.pdf]

Subject: RE: Reserved capacity credit ladder & GPU-index safeguard — Acme.ai

Naomi / team,

I ran three sensitivity scenarios and attached the model (gpu_sensitivity_model.csv). Short summary:
- Scenario A (one quarter +30% GPU spot index): estimated marginal cost impact to Redwood = 9% of quarterly committed spend; under our current margin targets this is within tolerable range if the quarterly rebate is capped at 15%.
- Scenario B (two consecutive low-util quarters at 45% utilization): cumulative credits hit ~12% annual committed revenue; this stresses the margin but is manageable if we keep a staged decommit with step-down fees in place.
- Scenario C (simultaneous shock: +30% GPU index and low utilization): worst-case modeled cumulative impact ~20%/year — we should not sign standard contracts with a rebate higher than 15% without exec approval.

Recommendation: Approve the 15% quarterly cap as written, keep the staged decommit at month 6 with a 2x step-down fee in month 7–9, and require any increase to the rebate/cap to be routed through Revenue Ops and CFO (David K.).

If Sales wants a pathway for exceptions, propose a two-tier approval ladder: (1) Revenue Ops (up to +5% incremental cap), (2) CFO for anything beyond that. I'll prep a one-page memo for leadership to sign off.

David Kim
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
[david@redwood.com]
